title: Upping the Game: Strengthening Critical Thinking in Debate in the World of AI
author: Stefan Bauschard
summary: Stefan Bauschard takes up debate coaches' worry that AI will erode the critical thinking debate builds. He demonstrates with Claude, Perplexity and ChatGPT that AI can already do typical prep homework in Congressional and Public Forum debate: summarize bills, generate arguments and questions, and draft responses and citations. His argument is that pretending students are not using AI is a failed strategy, so coaches should redesign assignments to treat AI output as a baseline. He lists nine assignments, such as ranking AI-generated arguments, finding the weakness in AI-cited evidence, and having students supply the third level of response. He concludes that AI does not threaten what debate teaches because the live skills of adaptation, refutation, and choosing where to win remain human. The piece is practical but written early in the generative-AI period and with a clearly enthusiastic stance.
points: AI can already complete traditional debate prep tasks such as bill summaries, argument lists, question lists and response tables.
Treating AI like extra teammates or coaches raises the quality of the game rather than replacing student thinking.
Redesigned assignments ask students to rank, critique and extend AI output and to explain their reasoning in class.
Having students find weaknesses in AI-cited evidence teaches both AI limits and how to attack opponents' evidence.
The core debate skills of adapting to opponents and judges, defending evidence and choosing where to win remain human.
quotes: This is not an unfair concern and resolving it requires changing preparation assignments, strengthening the expectations we have of our students, while permitting and even encouraging students to use AIs for “base line” work.

Common “homework” assignments include dividing the bills between the students and asking them to prepare summaries, lists of pro/con arguments, and questions that participants may want to ask in each of the model Congressional Debates they will participate in. AIs can complete those tasks with ease.

So, the question for debate coaches, like all teachers, is what should we ask our students to do that takes this as a given and helps advance them to the next level? Pretending that debaters aren’t using AIs to do their homework/prepare them for debates is not only a failed strategy but puts them at a competitive disadvantage relative to peers who are using it in such capacity.

(1) Use AI to generate list of 10 arguments in favor of _____. Then rank each argument in order from better to worse and come to class being ready to explain your ranking and different factors that influence your ranking.
As a teacher, use your own AI to generate a list of arguments and responses. In class, have the students generate the third level of response.
Without these changes, students will simply use AIs to complete old-fashioned/pre-AI World debate work and will be worse off for it. That’s a reality. We can, and should, do better.
